title: One Year Later
tagline: Look back on what you were made to do, how far you have come, and what you hope for.
hook: Under the cherry trees, a year after Noa arrived, everyone looks back. This last lesson combines the passive and causative, then shows how to talk about change and purpose.
goals: Say you were made to do something with 〜させられる
Show gradual change with 〜ようになる

points.title: 〜させられる
explain: Make the causative (読ませる) then turn it into the passive (読ませられる). For many u-verbs there is a shorter form: 読ます → 読まされる, 待つ → 待たされる. する becomes させられる.
It means someone forced you to do something, usually against your will: 毎日 そうじを させられた. The person who forced you takes に.

examples.ja: ぼくは|毎日|そうじを|させられました。
examples.en: I was made to clean every day.

examples.ja: 一時間も|待たされました。
examples.gloss: a whole hour|was made to wait
examples.en: I was kept waiting for an hour.

examples.ja: 先生に|作文を|書かされました。
examples.en: I was made to write an essay by the teacher.

points.tip: Say it as one word: 待たされる, 書かされる, 食べさせられる.
points.watch: It sounds unhappy. If you volunteered, use 〜させてもらう instead.

points.title: 〜ようになる
points.formula: dictionary / potential form + ようになる
points.gist: A gradual change in ability or habit.
explain: Dictionary form or potential form + ようになる means that something that was not the case has now become the case: 日本語が 話せるように なりました (I have come to be able to speak Japanese).
The negative is 〜なくなる: 食べられなく なった. It describes change over time, not a decision.

examples.ja: 日本語が|話せるように|なりました。
examples.gloss: Japanese (subject)|to be able to speak|has become
examples.en: I have come to be able to speak Japanese.

examples.ja: だんだん|早く|起きられるように|なりました。
examples.gloss: gradually|early|to be able to get up|became
examples.en: Gradually I came to be able to get up early.

points.tip: ようになる = the "before and after" of an ability.
points.watch: ようになる is a change that happens. ようにする is your effort.

points.title: 〜ように（purpose）
explain: Put ように after a dictionary or potential form to show the purpose or hope: また 会えるように、手紙を 書きます (I will write so that we can meet again). The verb before ように is usually not fully under your control.
The negative is 〜ないように: わすれないように メモします (I note it so that I won't forget).

examples.ja: また|会えるように、|手紙を|書きます。
examples.gloss: again|so that we can meet|letter (object)|I will write
examples.en: I will write letters so that we can meet again.

examples.ja: わすれないように、|メモします。
examples.gloss: so that I don't forget|I will take notes
examples.en: I'll note it down so I don't forget.

points.tip: Use ように for outcomes you hope for and ために for outcomes you control.
points.watch: Do not use ように with a volitional verb. Say 行くために, not 行くように.

日本へ 行ったように、貯金します。
